question: Why do these two comparisons produce different results?
options: Both print true because Strings always compare by content
Both print false because == never works on Strings
a == b is true because literals share the same interned String object, while a == c is false because new String() creates a separate object
explanation: Java interns String literals, so a and b (both literal 'cat') refer to the same pooled object, making a == b true. new String('cat') explicitly creates a new, distinct object, so a == c is false even though the content is equal.
